title: Quantized Photocurrents in Gapless Topological Matter
authors: Byunghoon Kim, Tenzin Norden, Mohammad Yahyavi, Kaustuv Manna, Tyler A. Cochran, Zi-Jia Cheng, Xian P. Yang, Yu-Xiao Jiang, Xiangyu Luo, Payman Kazemikhah, Areeq Hasan, Vladimir N. Strocov, Sergey Shilov, Ilya Belopolski, Claudia Felser, Md Shafayat Hossain, Rohit P. Prasankumar, Guoqing Chang, M. Zahid Hasan, Prashant Padmanabhan
abstract: The quantum Hall effect in gapped systems represents a defining signature of nontrivial topology. Realizing this principle in gapless matter has remained a central challenge in quantum materials. Chiral topological semimetals provide a unique platform to achieve this aim via symmetry-protected multifold crossings that act as Berry-curvature monopoles. When optical transitions are confined to a single multifold node, the resulting circular photogalvanic effect is predicted to be quantized in terms of the topological charge of the node. In real materials, however, this phenomenon remains experimentally elusive, obscured by trivial band transitions, the energy separation between the node pairs, and their relative positions with respect to the Fermi level. Here we observe a quantized circular photogalvanic effect in the chiral topological semimetal Rh0.95Ni0.05Si. Ni substitution opens a photon-energy window dominated by interband optical transitions at the Γ-point multifold node. This allows circularly polarized near- to mid-infrared pulses to drive a helicity-odd terahertz response that manifests three hallmarks of quantization: a sharp onset, a wavelength-independent plateau governed by the magnitude of monopole charge, and an abrupt cutoff imposed by Pauli blocking. Our work establishes an all-optical analogue for the quantum Hall effect and a new paradigm for topological quantization in gapless matter.
summary: The paper reports the observation of a quantized circular photogalvanic effect in the chiral semimetal $	ext{Rh}_{0.95}	ext{Ni}_{0.05}	ext{Si}$. By tuning the material via Ni doping, the authors isolate optical transitions originating from a single topological multifold node. This results in a characteristic THz emission plateau whose magnitude quantizes according to the node's topological charge, establishing a novel measurement paradigm for topology in gapless matter.
main_problem: The central challenge is realizing a quantized physical response, analogous to the Quantum Hall Effect (QHE), in gapless topological matter.
main_result: The authors experimentally observe and theoretically confirm a quantized circular photogalvanic effect plateau in $	ext{Rh}_{0.95}	ext{Ni}_{0.05}	ext{Si}$, establishing an all-optical analogue for the QHE.
method: The study combines first-principles calculations of the CPGE tensor ($ oldsymbol{ eta}(\omega)$) with THz emission spectroscopy using circularly polarized near- to mid-infrared pulses.
model_or_system: The system is a chiral topological semimetal, $	ext{Rh}_{0.95}	ext{Ni}_{0.05}	ext{Si}$, which possesses symmetry-protected multifold crossings acting as Berry-curvature monopoles at the $\Gamma$-point.
key_observables: Quantized plateau height of the THz emission (calibrated response product $ eta	au$), and polarization dependence dominated by the $A_1$ term ($\propto \sin(2\phi)$).
important_parameters: The effective monopole charge ($C_{	ext{exp}} \simeq 2.37$) compared to the theoretical integer charge ($C=2$). The optical window is tuned by Ni doping.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the observed signal is dominated by transitions localized around a single multifold node, which is achieved through chemical tuning (Ni substitution).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the confinement of p-polarized THz emission to a spectral window, show the plateau height vs. wavelength matching theory, and confirm the dominance of the $A_1$ polarization component.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical link between QHE topology and CPGE in gapless systems; it details how Ni doping isolates a single optical node; experimental THz measurements reveal the quantized plateau signature; and DFT calculations reproduce this quantization by modeling the $\Gamma$-point contribution while suppressing competing $R$-point contributions.
why_interesting: This work provides an all-optical, measurable analogue to topological invariants (like Chern numbers) in a solid-state material using nonlinear optics, which is highly relevant for understanding quantum transport phenomena beyond standard band theory.
